expectations.text: Flags that the runbook never states who it is for or what the reader already knows
expectations.evidence: No finding names the missing audience or assumed knowledge. #11 only says the title doesn't say 'runbook'; #6 suggests adding owner/on-call links, which is not the reader or their prior knowledge.

expectations.text: Flags that the rollback procedure, the thing a reader of a runbook needs, is not at the top and is split across two sections
expectations.evidence: #1: 'Combine the two sections into one rollback procedure'; #11: 'put the incident procedures near the top, since that's what people will open it for.'

expectations.text: Flags that the heading 'Rollback is automatic' contradicts its body, which describes a manual kubectl command
expectations.evidence: #2: 'The heading "Rollback is automatic" is wrong. The section describes a manual command.'

expectations.text: Flags that the processor timeout is stated as 30 seconds in one place and 60 seconds in others
expectations.evidence: #3 lists line 13 '30 seconds', line 29 `processor_timeout_seconds: 60`, line 40 '60 seconds'.

expectations.text: Flags that worker, consumer and job runner name the same component, or asks whether they are one component
expectations.evidence: #5 'One component, three names' and open question 'Are worker, consumer and job runner the same process?'

expectations.text: Flags at least one pronoun ('it') whose antecedent is ambiguous
expectations.evidence: No finding addresses an ambiguous 'it' ('it times out', 'It should recover'); #4 quotes 'It should recover' but critiques only missing dashboard/threshold details.

expectations.text: Flags the 'in the YAML file, not in the Helm chart' contrast as unexplained or as implying an unstated rule
expectations.evidence: #8: 'It says to set the retry count in the YAML file and not in the Helm chart, but not why (does Helm override it? ...)'

expectations.text: Flags writer-serving content: the 'This section will discuss' opener, the migration history, or 'It's worth noting'
expectations.evidence: #6: 'The monolith split and the move to Kubernetes don't help anyone running the service... Also cut "This section will discuss".'

expectations.text: Orders findings with reader/contract problems before structure problems before sentence-level problems
expectations.evidence: Ordered by severity (Blockers, Other issues). Structure issues (#1, #2) come first; reader/contract-type issues (#6 overview, #11 title) come late and are mixed with others. No reader/contract section precedes structure.

expectations.text: Gives a concrete rewrite for most findings, not only a description of the problem
expectations.evidence: Concrete replacement text only for #1 (numbered steps), #2 (new heading), #10 (example sentence), #11 (new title), plus a structure outline. #3, #4, #5, #7, #8 give directions or questions ('Find the real value', 'say so', lists of what's missing) rather than rewritten text; under half of 11 findings have a concrete rewrite.
